ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: The Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, including its provisions on individuals with significant control and the associated regulations, requires covered Alberta corporations to maintain an internal register. The federal Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, and regulations govern reporting entities and applicable beneficial-ownership identification and verification duties; they do not create a general public federal UBO register for Alberta corporations. Alberta corporate registers of individuals with significant control are not a general public-search register. Confirm current statutory text and applicability at filing.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Apply risk-based customer due diligence, identity verification, beneficial-owner identification, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth inquiry where risk warrants, and ongoing monitoring. Canadian reporting entities must comply with the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and regulations, including applicable politically exposed person and head-of-international-organization measures. Screen against applicable Canadian sanctions under the United Nations Act, Special Economic Measures Act, Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, and Criminal Code terrorism measures, and against UN Security Council lists. OFAC screening is not a universal Canadian statutory requirement but may be contractually or commercially required for U.S. nexus, U.S. persons, or U.S. payment rails. Investigate potential matches and document disposition; do not treat a name-only match as conclusive.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry services are delivered through authorized Alberta registry agents; the Alberta Corporate Registry does not provide a single public online incorporation portal equivalent to a direct self-service filing portal. Use an authorized registry agent and obtain the required Alberta NUANS report for a named corporation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must comply with the Alberta Business Corporations Act and regulations, be distinguishable and not misleading, and use an authorized legal element such as Limited, Ltd., Corporation, Corp., Incorporated, Inc., or, if the corporation is validly formed as an unlimited liability corporation, Unlimited Liability Corporation or ULC. English or French names are generally used for Alberta corporate filings. A translated or transliterated version does not itself establish name availability; obtain registry-agent confirmation for any non-Latin or additional-language name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, banker, banking, trust, trustee, insurance, insurer, university, college, or other regulated or misleading terms may be restricted or require consent or approval under applicable legislation.
Government, Crown, royal, provincial, federal, municipal, or other official-affiliation terms may be prohibited or require consent.
Words implying an association with a regulated profession, public authority, or licensed activity may require approval or may be refused if misleading.
Names that are identical or deceptively similar to existing names, reserved names, or protected trademarks, or that are obscene or otherwise contrary to law, may be rejected.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A NUANS report is generally usable for Alberta filing for 90 days from its report date; confirm the report's expiry and filing requirements with the registry agent. If a name is rejected, obtain the written refusal and reason, correct the name or provide supporting evidence of consent, entitlement, or distinctiveness, and resubmit through an authorized registry agent with a fresh report if the original has expired. Request reconsideration or pursue any available statutory review or judicial remedy only after confirming the applicable decision-maker, deadline, and procedure with Alberta counsel; a name refusal does not carry a general automatic appeal right or a guaranteed extension.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: An Alberta corporation must maintain a registered office in Alberta and a records office in Alberta as required by the Business Corporations Act. A commercial registered-office service may be acceptable if it provides a valid physical Alberta address, accepts service, maintains required records or access arrangements, and satisfies registry and bank requirements. A mailbox-only address is inadequate. For medical-device manufacturing, a virtual registered office does not replace the actual manufacturing, quality-system, licensing, importation, distribution, or establishment requirements applicable under the federal Food and Drugs Act and Medical Devices Regulations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No Alberta incorporation rule establishes a numerical inspection probability. Risk is low for routine corporate registry filing but may increase materially if Health Canada licensing, compliance verification, product complaints, recalls, importation, or quality-system issues arise. Do not represent an unsupported percentage as a statutory or regulator-published likelihood.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss. 12-16, 23, 101-104, 112 and 123, together with the Business Corporations Regulations (Alberta)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction, or an accredited Alberta Corporate Registry Agent
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Alberta Form 1) under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the Alberta ULC may issue shares with no par value for such consideration as the directors determine, and no escrow account deposit is prescribed for this entity type.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF ABC UNLIMITED LIABILITY CORPORATION: WHEREAS the Alberta Corporate Registry has issued a Certificate of Incorporation and the initial directors have been named in the Articles. RESOLVED: 1. That the subscription for the initial common shares set out in the Articles is accepted, and share certificates shall be issued to subscribers upon receipt of full consideration. 2. That the registered office be fixed at 000, 12345 102 Avenue NW, Edmonton, Alberta, T5K 0B3, and the Corporate Registry be notified of any change. 3. That [Name] be appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, each to hold office until the next annual meeting or until successors are elected. 4. That the General Operating By-law No. 1 be adopted provisionally. 5. That management be authorized to open bank accounts, obtain licences, and complete all ancillary filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and NUANS corporate name search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through Service Alberta online portal or a licensed Alberta Corporate Registry Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed corporate names and obtain a Computerized Name Search (NUANS) report. The name must include 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC'. Reserve the approved name for 90 days and include the reservation with the Articles of Incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or conflicts with an existing name, submit a revised proposed name with a fresh NUANS search; if the reservation lapses, re-file the name reservation before filing Articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and attest Articles of Incorporation and director consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator, legal counsel, notary public, or commissioned Alberta legal adviser
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the prescribed Alberta Articles of Incorporation, including the ULC name, authorized share structure, restrictions on business if any, initial directors, and registered office location. The incorporator executes the Articles before a witness or notary, and each initial director executes a written consent to act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Revise and re-attest defective schedules; obtain new director consents if the director slate is changed before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Articles and receive Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, or accredited Corporate Registry Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Articles, Notice of Registered Office, Notice of Directors, NUANS report, and statutory filing fee. Pay the prescribed fee using an accepted method, and the Registry will issue a Certificate of Incorporation stating the legal name, incorporation number, and effective date.
required_dossiers: NUANS search report or name reservation confirmation
Notice of registered office and first directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a query or deficiency letter, respond within the specified period, correct the stated defect, pay any resubmission fee, and resubmit; if refused, prepare amended Articles and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-incorporation tax registration and municipal business licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration, municipal business licensing authority, and Workers' Compensation Board
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Certificate of Incorporation, obtain a CRA Business Number with corporate income tax, GST/HST, and payroll accounts. Register with the Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration where required, obtain a municipal business licence for the Edmonton facility, and open a WCB account if workers will be employed.
required_dossiers: Registered office address and corporate records
Anticipated revenue, payroll, and employment information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA or municipal processing is delayed, contact the applicable enquiry desk with the registration reference number and Certificate of Incorporation, and file all missing elections or declarations within 30 days of the delay notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate governance start-up: minute books, by-laws, officers, and banking
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors, corporate secretary, and Alberta Corporate Registry for filings of changes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting, adopt the first board resolution, issue share certificates, elect officers, provisionally adopt the general operating by-law, ratify the opening of bank accounts, and complete the minute book and share register. File annual returns and any changes to registered office or directors at the Alberta Corporate Registry.
required_dossiers: First board meeting minutes and resolutions
Share subscription agreement and share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry rejects an annual return or notice of change, re-file electronically after correcting the data; amend organizational records in the minute book to ensure consistency with the last accepted filing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Health Canada – Medical Devices Directorate (Medical Devices Bureau); Alberta Municipal Affairs Safety Services for facility and fire safety conformance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) under the Medical Devices Regulations (SOR/98-282), together with applicable Medical Device Licence, municipal business licence, and Alberta building/fire safety permitting

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Screening under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act; a Full EIA Report is required only if prescribed activities, such as large-scale metal finishing or solvent cleaning, exceed Schedule thresholds
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must meet Alberta EPEA approval limits and municipal sewer use bylaws; VOC emissions must comport with Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives and CEPA 1999 National Pollutant Release Inventory reporting thresholds; hazardous waste handling must comply with the Waste Control Regulation (Alta. Reg. 192/1996)

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Alberta Fire Code certification and local fire marshal inspection for the assembly and cleanroom areas; structural load approval by a professional engineer for equipment mezzanines or heavy device stations; workplace clearance under the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Code, including emergency response planning, machine guarding, and industrial hygiene verification

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada, official business portal: CRA 'My Business Account' at https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html; Alberta corporate income tax is administered by CRA under a tax collection agreement with Alberta Treasury Board and Finance; customs and export border controls are administered by the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) at https://www.cbsa-asfc.gc.ca. Alberta has no provincial sales tax authority.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Alberta ULC must first be incorporated or registered with the Alberta Corporate Registry; the foreign parent then obtains the statutory Canadian tax identifier by applying for a CRA Business Number (BN) through Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or CRA Business Registration On-line (BRO). The 9-digit BN with program account suffixes (RC for federal corporate income tax, RT for GST/HST, RM for payroll/import-export) serves as the TIN/VAT ID. A non-resident-owned ULC carrying on manufacturing activities, holding inventory, or maintaining employees in Alberta must register for the RC, RT, and RM program accounts, file T2 corporate income tax returns, and open an RM customs account with CBSA if it imports or exports goods. CRA will request the certificate of incorporation, Alberta registration extract, articles of amendment, and proof of registered head office address before issuing the BN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No domestic Canadian check-the-box election exists under the Income Tax Act; an Alberta ULC is generally a taxable Canadian corporation and is assessed at the entity level. However, the ULC is eligible for pass-through treatment for U.S. federal tax purposes if all U.S. shareholders elect to treat it as a disregarded entity on IRS Form 8832. CRA does not recognize this election for Canadian tax, and will continue to treat the ULC as a separate person subject to Canadian corporate income tax, GST/HST, and Part XIII withholding tax on dividends. Hybrid mismatch rules under ITA sections 18.2 and 18.3 may deny a deduction for a ULC interest, royalty, or management fee payment that is deductible in Canada but not included in the foreign owner's income solely because of the check-the-box classification, unless a 'fully taxed' exception or treaty limitation applies. A ULC may also be entitled to benefits under the Canada-U.S. Tax Convention as a 'resident of Canada' if it is liable to tax in Canada on its worldwide income; no paper election is mandatory to claim treaty benefits, though Form NR303 can be filed to evidence residency for reduced withholding.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) - a value-added tax administered federally by CRA. Alberta has no provincial sales tax, so the only applicable indirect tax on domestic taxable supplies in Alberta is the 5% federal GST; supplies exported outside Canada are zero-rated at 0% GST.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000. A person, including a non-resident entity, making taxable supplies in Canada in the course of carrying on business in Canada must register for GST/HST if the person's annual worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000. The threshold is measured on a calendar-quarter-look-back and prospective basis; zero-rated exports count as taxable supplies for this purpose. Once the threshold is exceeded, registration under CRA GST/HST account (RT) is mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time e-invoicing or fiscal digital stamping regime currently exists in Canada. CRA accepts electronic invoices and records if they meet the GST/HST invoice requirements under section 221 of the Excise Tax Act (supplier identity, GST number, date, taxable amount, tax rate, and tax payable). Export declarations are filed electronically through the CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) or the modernized CBSA Assessment and Revenue Management (CARM) portal; there is no API-based real-time clearance or digital stamping for ordinary GST/HST invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A GST/HST registrant may zero-rate the supply of surgical laparoscopy towers and related 4K endoscopic cameras, monitors, and trocars if the goods are delivered to a foreign hospital or distributor outside Canada and are exported by the supplier 'as soon after the supply is made as is reasonable' under section 21 of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act. The supply must be made to a non-resident and the goods must not be acquired for use, consumption, or supply in Canada. Optional software or configuration services exported with the original hardware may be zero-rated as a supply of movable property exported under section 9 (basic zero-rating) or as a supply to a non-resident under section 7, subject to the service being performed for a non-resident outside Canada for exclusive use outside Canada. The ULC must obtain and retain clear documentary evidence of shipment, destination, and foreign buyer status to support the 0% rate and the corresponding input tax credits (ITCs) for GST paid on raw materials, components, and overheads.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Form B13A or electronic CERS Record)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing Canadian point of departure and foreign destination
Commercial Invoice with full product description, HS classification, quantities, and value
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank SWIFT/TT transfer confirmation showing payment received in Canadian or foreign currency in a Canadian account
Packing List with serial numbers, weights, and unit counts
Signed Export Sales Contract or Purchase Order from the non-resident buyer
Forwarder's Cargo Receipt or Carrier Certificate of Export
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may reassess a GST/HST return within four years of the filing date, but where a zero-rating claim is fraudulent or involves misrepresentation attributable to negligence, carelessness, or wilful default, reassessment is unrestricted. If the ULC fails to produce satisfactory evidence of export, CRA will recharacterise the supply as taxable at 5% GST, assess additional tax, interest, and penalties, and may deny the ITCs claimed. Gross negligence penalties under the Excise Tax Act can amount to 50% of the understated net tax; false statements or omissions can attract civil penalties up to 25% of the amount. Criminal prosecution under section 327 of the Excise Tax Act can result in fines up to 200% of the evaded tax, imprisonment up to five years, or both. CBSA may also issue Corporate Administrative Monetary Penalties (CAMPs) for inaccurate export declarations, including omissions of mandated shipping particulars.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a floating exchange rate regime with full convertibility for current account transactions under the Foreign Exchange Act. Capital account transactions are generally open for corporate entities, though large or sensitive investments may require prior review by the Bank of Canada or OSFI. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is permitted subject to withholding tax obligations and beneficial ownership reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds to the Bank of Canada is required. Exporters may retain foreign currency or convert to CAD at their discretion. All export transactions must be reported to CBSA and CRA with supporting commercial invoices, packing lists, and shipping documents for customs and tax compliance.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Cross-border EMI operations via fintech platforms are restricted in Canada due to FINTRAC registration and OSFI oversight. Offshore digital EMIs require licensing through a Canadian bank or authorized partner, with strict AML controls and no unlicensed issuance permitted.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and key personnel must attend in-person KYC interviews and account opening at tier-one banks. Remote video KYC is permitted for ongoing account management but not for initial corporate account setup.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership not fully disclosed or source of funds from high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate charter, articles of incorporation, beneficial ownership certificate, director profiles, and audited financial statements

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital from shareholders is transferred via SWIFT MT103 wires using purpose code 'Capital Contribution' or 'Shareholder Loan'. Verification protocols include matching beneficiary name to entity registration, supporting board resolutions, and foreign exchange transaction reports (Form T1135 if applicable).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements use SWIFT MT103 for direct payments or commercial letters of credit under UCP 600. Purpose codes are 'Trade Payment' or 'Export Proceeds'. All disbursements require matching commercial invoices, packing lists, and proof of export compliance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Currency swaps and cross-currency basis swaps

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation or of the last annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee CAD 50; continued non-filing for two years may lead to administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the balance owing, plus 1% per month up to 12 months, with potential criminal penalties for wilful non-filing

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Private corporations under the Alberta Business Corporations Act are not required to appoint an auditor if all shareholders entitled to vote consent to the waiver on an annual basis and the corporation is not a reporting issuer; otherwise, an independent auditor must be appointed.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public enterprises or ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for private corporations, in accordance with Canadian GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not currently mandate a separate UBO annual confirmation; the annual return confirms the registered office and current directors. Share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Members, and any changes in significant control should be reflected in corporate records as proposed under Alberta's significant individual register regime (when in force).

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SR&ED ITC 35% refundable for eligible CCPCs (15% non-refundable for large corporations); accelerated CCA on Class 43 manufacturing machinery (30% declining balance) and Class 29; GST/HST input tax recovery; no provincial M&P preferential rate in Alberta. Non-resident-controlled ULC cannot claim the small business deduction.
